question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 16 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 23 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 10 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Work** (LCM of 16, 23, 10) = 1840 units.

**Combined Efficiency** = (1840/16) + (1840/23) + (1840/10) = 115 + 80 + 184 = 379.

**Time Taken** = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 1840 ÷ 379.

**Mixed Fraction** = 4(324/379) hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 4(324/379) hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Pipe A** = 16 hours, **Pipe B** = 23 hours, **Pipe C** = 10 hours.

**Formula Used:** Total Time = Total Work ÷ (Sum of individual efficiencies)

 
 

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 

 Pipe A 16 hr 1840 115 

 Pipe B 23 hr 80 

 Pipe C 10 hr 184 

⇒ Total Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 115 + 80 + 184 = 379

⇒ Time Taken = 1840 ÷ 379

⇒ Time Taken = 4 with Remainder 324

⇒ Result = 4(324/379) hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4(324/379) hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Concept
 

If a pipe fills a tank in 'x' hours, then the part filled in 1 hour is 1/x. For outlet pipes (leakage), the efficiency is taken as negative.

Combined Time Formula
 

For two pipes A and B, the time taken together is (A × B) ÷ (A + B). For three pipes, it is (A × B × C) ÷ (AB + BC + CA).</p
